title: wmem: Introducing ws_free()
description:
Introducing `ws_free()`.

Similar logic to `ws_strdup()`.

ws_free(ptr) = wmem_free(NULL, ptr)

~enhancement

notes.body: Could also update the six instances `wmem_free(NULL, ptr)` in the code to utilize this

Definitely on the fence about this.  Agree that the mass search/replace should be done, but that even more exposes that we don't really have a "ws scope".  I was originally going to suggest that ws_free() potentially move to wmem_strutl.h, because I thought it paired well with ws_strdup_printf and friends.  But as this search/replace shows there are many places that use "NULL scoped memory" with functions that aren't ws_ prefixed.
Does this somehow "help" Coverity understand the internals of Wireshark memory allocation?

so when I was working on !23746 I realized that while `ws_strdup()` is used and exists, there is no equivalent for `wmem_free()` so then I thought let's add `ws_free()`. At that moment I did no realize the almost 500 occurrences to replace. Whether some or many of those are a concern due to "NULL scoped memory" is a good question and it would need more analysis... and not using ws_ prefixed functions is another round of discussion.

Overall, this change has no effect on Coverity. Coverity needs a custom model file for WS memory handling functions to eliminate a lot of false positive resource leak warnings... I have been looking into it but the basic (free) access is very limited...
I'm not a fan, much churn for no real gain, IMHO.

Well, there are a lot of ws_ prefixed definitions around with mixed use. I thought adding `ws_free()` would logically fit into the same concept. Yes, it does not add much value but `ws_strdup()` does not add either.

If we use `ws_strdup(src)` instead of `wmem_strdup(NULL, src)` then it would suggest to use `ws_free(ptr)` instead `wmem_free(NULL, ptr)`.

Indeed, it's more cosmetic...
IMHO we should not have introduced ws_strdup() in the first place.

That might be a valid point :smile: 

But then how about:

`#define ws_strdup(src) wmem_strdup(NULL, src)`

`#define ws_strndup(src, len) wmem_strndup(NULL, src, len)`

`#define ws_strdup_printf(...) wmem_strdup_printf(NULL, __VA_ARGS__)`

`#define ws_strdup_vprintf(fmt, ap) wmem_strdup_vprintf(NULL, fmt, ap)`


For all of these functions we shall use `wmem_free(NULL, ...)` in general because they don't have their logical pair of `ws_free()`.

For me it's just simply confusing that since we already have these definitions for a slight simplifications when allocator is NULL but we do not want to consistently use/add one for freeing up memory.

Occurences:
- `ws_strdup()`: 102 results in 22 files
- `ws_strndup()`: 1 result  in 1 file (wmem_strutl.h) but `wmem_strndup(NULL, ...)` 4 results in 4 files
- `ws_strdup_printf()`: 1376 results in 254 files
- `ws_strdup_vprintf()`: 20 results in 14 files

Memory freeing:
- `ws_strdup()`: I don't see how those were freed up
- `ws_strndup()` is not used
- `ws_strdup_printf()` seems to use `g_free()` in some cases (some other case I don't see how it was freed up)
- `ws_strdup_vprintf()` seems to use `g_free()`


**However**, after further analysis the whole code I can see that `wmem_free(NULL, ..)` is used for a lot of other functions to without the ws_ prefix, e.g. `wmem_strconcat(NULL, ...)`, `val_to_str(NULL,...)`, `val_to_str_ext(NULL,...)`, `address_to_str(NULL, ...)` and in some cases `g_free()` is used instead.

Hence, my conclusion aligns with your view that there is no real advantage to introducing `ws_free()`.

**All agreed to close this MR then?**
okay, so close it then. :grin:

+/**
+ * @brief Convenience macro for freeing allocated memory using the NULL allocator.

+ */
+#define ws_free(ptr) wmem_free(NULL, ptr)
